clinical_category: Pulmonary rehabilitation referral - evidence-based COPD care
blueprint_topic: Care coordination and referral to interdisciplinary pulmonary rehabilitation
stem: A nurse discusses pulmonary rehabilitation with a client who has stable COPD. Which description of pulmonary rehabilitation is accurate?

options.A: It is a comprehensive program that includes individualized exercise training and self-management education and can improve exercise capacity and health-related quality of life
options.B: It consists primarily of medication adjustment and excludes structured exercise training
options.C: It is recommended only after a client develops end-stage COPD with severe lung-function impairment
options.D: It has no established role for adults with stable COPD unless they were recently hospitalized

rationale: A is correct. The 2023 official American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline defines pulmonary rehabilitation as a comprehensive intervention that includes patient-tailored therapies such as exercise training, education, and behavior change; core components include structured, progressive, individually tailored exercise training and self-management education. For adults with stable COPD, ATS gives a strong recommendation for pulmonary rehabilitation based on moderate-quality evidence and notes improvements in exercise capacity and health-related quality of life. B, C, and D conflict with the guideline: exercise is a core component, the stable-COPD recommendation is not limited to end-stage disease, and pulmonary rehabilitation is recommended both for stable COPD and after hospitalization for an exacerbation.
educational_objective: Recognize pulmonary rehabilitation as an interdisciplinary, exercise- and education-based intervention recommended for adults with stable COPD to improve important functional and quality-of-life outcomes.
source_document_title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation for Adults with Chronic Respiratory Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline
source_version_date: Official ATS Clinical Practice Guideline approved May 2023; current ATS guideline resource accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: Introduction: pulmonary rehabilitation definition and core components include structured progressive individualized exercise training and self-management education. Summary of Recommendations, Recommendation 1: for adults with stable COPD, recommend participation in pulmonary rehabilitation (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence). Question 1 rationale: pulmonary rehabilitation improves exercise capacity and health-related quality of life and reduces dyspnea.
source_claim_supported: The current official ATS guideline directly supports pulmonary rehabilitation's exercise/education components and its strong recommendation and functional/quality-of-life benefits for adults with stable COPD.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items), within Safe and Effective Care Environment; this item tests coordination/referral to an evidence-based interdisciplinary service.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The generic ATS homepage was replaced by the current official 2023 ATS pulmonary-rehabilitation guideline with exact definition, core-component, and stable-COPD recommendation locators. The vague psychosocial-support claim and overbroad disease-severity wording were replaced by directly supported components and outcomes.
audit_findings: The original ATS root URL did not provide an exact claim locator.
The official 2023 ATS guideline directly defines pulmonary rehabilitation and identifies individualized exercise training and self-management education as core components.
The guideline strongly recommends pulmonary rehabilitation for adults with stable COPD and directly supports exercise-capacity and health-related-quality-of-life benefit.
The final options exclude the unsupported implication that pulmonary rehabilitation is restricted to the most severe COPD or only to the post-hospital period.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible option, no cueing, no unsupported severity threshold, and no unresolved conflict.
